questions.q: What is the key difference between FIXED and INCLUDE/EXCLUDE?
options: There is no real difference — they are interchangeable syntax for the same behavior
INCLUDE and EXCLUDE ignore filters, while FIXED always respects every filter
FIXED only works with numeric fields, while INCLUDE and EXCLUDE only work with dates
FIXED is independent of the view; INCLUDE and EXCLUDE compute relative to whatever's currently on the view
questions.explain: FIXED computes at a grain that has nothing to do with the view's shelves. INCLUDE and EXCLUDE add or remove dimensions relative to whatever's currently on the view, so editing the view can change their results.

questions.q: What does { INCLUDE [Order ID] : COUNTD([Product Name]) } compute, before any re-aggregation by the view?
options: The total count of all products across the entire data source
The average sales per order
The count of distinct products per order — finer detail than a view grained only by Region
The count of orders per product
questions.explain: INCLUDE adds Order ID to the calculation's grain, computing distinct products per order — finer than a Region-level view — which the view then re-aggregates (often with AVG) up to its own grain.

questions.q: On a view grained by Category and Sub-Category, what does { EXCLUDE [Sub-Category] : SUM([Sales]) } return for each row?
options: Zero, because EXCLUDE removes the measure from the calculation
The grand total across all categories combined
The same value as a plain SUM([Sales]) with no change
That row's parent Category total, repeated across every sub-category belonging to that category
questions.explain: EXCLUDE removes Sub-Category from the calculation's grain, so it computes at the Category level instead — giving each sub-category row its parent category's total, the building block for a percent-of-parent ratio.

questions.q: Which expression computes a 'percent of parent category' ratio using EXCLUDE?
options: { INCLUDE [Category] : SUM([Sales]) }
SUM([Sales]) / { EXCLUDE [Sub-Category] : SUM([Sales]) }
{ EXCLUDE [Sub-Category] : SUM([Sales]) } / SUM([Sales])
{ FIXED [Sub-Category] : SUM([Sales]) }
questions.explain: Dividing the row's own sales by the EXCLUDE-computed parent category total gives each sub-category's share of its category — without a second query or table calculation.

questions.q: If you add a new dimension to the view (say, Segment), what happens to an existing INCLUDE or EXCLUDE calculation's result, compared to a FIXED calculation?
options: Neither changes — all LOD expressions are permanently locked once written
Only FIXED changes; INCLUDE and EXCLUDE are always constant regardless of the view
The INCLUDE/EXCLUDE result can change, because it's computed relative to the view; a FIXED result mostly stays the same, because it's independent of the view
Both change identically, because all LOD expressions behave the same way
questions.explain: INCLUDE and EXCLUDE are defined relative to the view's grain, so editing the view can change what they compute. FIXED ignores the view's dimensions entirely, so it mostly doesn't move when you edit the view.
